diagnostics.title: Logs and diagnostics
diagnostics.summary: Check server health, investigate errors and collect diagnostic information
diagnostics.body:
Administrators manage the server and integrations. They can inspect logs and collect diagnostics, but cannot view student records.

## Find the right section

- **Status:** service health, pending events, version, uptime, memory, disk space, latest backup and portal address. “Collect diagnostics” downloads an archive for a developer with logs, redacted settings and system information.
- **Log:** switch between “Logs”, “Events” and “Errors”. Select an entry to see its request code and error details. With no entry selected, you can temporarily enable more detailed logging for a section.
- **Integrations:** check messaging apps, AI, the LiveKit call server and other connected services. This section also contains AI settings.
- **Backups:** create and restore [backups](/admin/help/backups).
- **Settings:** manage [portal settings](/admin/help/settings) without editing .env.

On a computer, use the sidebar; on a phone, use the bottom navigation bar. Help is at the bottom of the sidebar or under ☰ on a phone. Select your name to open “My account”, choose a theme or language, or sign out.

## Investigate a problem

1. Open “Integrations” and run a connection check.
2. Search the log around the time of the problem.
3. In “Status”, choose “Collect diagnostics” and send the archive to the developer with the error code and steps to reproduce it.

## Server commands

If the installer was used, the server provides the following commands:

- `sudo teacherbox status` — show the running version and service status;
- `sudo teacherbox logs backend` — view backend logs, including when the portal will not open;
- `sudo teacherbox update` — install an update while keeping data and settings;
- `sudo teacherbox backups` — copy backups to a server directory;
- `sudo teacherbox reset` — delete the database, files, server backups and accounts, then start a fresh installation. Settings in .env are kept.

The bundled Caddy service obtains an HTTPS certificate for TEACHERBOX_DOMAIN automatically. If it cannot, check that the domain points to the server and ports 80 and 443 are open. View its logs with `sudo teacherbox logs caddy`.

backups.title: Backups and portal address
backups.summary: Create and restore backups, and check the portal’s public address
backups.body:
## Backups

Open “Backups” to view existing backups, choose “Back up now” or restore a backup. Only the teacher can download backups because they contain student data. The teacher also manages the Google Drive connection.

Backups in Google Drive appear here too. Download one to the server before restoring it from the server list.

Retention is set in “Settings” → “Backups” → “Days to keep backups”, with a default of 14 days. After creating a new backup, the portal removes older backups of every kind from both the server and Google Drive.

## Restore a backup

1. Open the backup’s ⋮ menu and choose “Restore…”.
2. Enter your administrator password.
3. Keep the page open while the portal backs up its current state, restarts and restores the selected backup.

Let the teacher know before restoring: data added after the backup will be replaced. Afterwards, sign in with the password that was in use when the backup was created.

Automatic restart requires the container policy `restart: unless-stopped`, which is included in the portal’s Compose files. Outside Docker, restoration runs the next time the portal starts.

## Portal address

Find the public address in “Status” → “Portal address”. It is used for invitation links, bot messages, calendar subscriptions and Google and Yandex callback URLs. If TEACHERBOX_PUBLIC_URL sets the address, it is read-only in the portal.

settings.title: Portal settings
settings.summary: Files, proxies, sign-in and backups, with no restart
settings.body:
“Settings” is laid out in cards: “Homework files”, “Network and proxies”, “Sign-in and sessions”, “Messages” and “Backups”. Each value shows its source: the default, .env or a value saved here.

## Apply changes

1. Edit the values you need. Changed fields are marked.
2. Choose “Save” and enter your administrator password.
3. Most settings take effect straight away. If a field says “Takes effect after the portal restarts”, the portal restarts on its own and is unavailable to everyone for about a minute.

Values saved here override .env. Choose “Use .env value” to remove an override.

Portal and board backups run once a day. Use the switch to turn a backup on or off and pick its time, in the teacher’s time zone. If .env sets a different cron schedule, it is shown as it is and you can still change it.

New sign-in and lockout limits apply from the next sign-in; open sessions carry on.

## Settings only in .env

The “Only in .env” card shows the current values of settings you cannot change here: the domain, port and container resources, video calls, accounts, the access token secret, logging and the restart after a restore. Passwords and secrets are never shown, only whether they are set. To change one, run sudo teacherbox config on the server: it opens .env, and the portal restarts with the new values once you save. If one of these settings was saved in the portal earlier, choose “Remove saved value” to go back to the .env value.

## Moved to the teacher’s settings

The time zone, currency, lesson rules, portal address, bots and Google connections are now set by the teacher in their own “Settings”. If .env still contains their variables, the page lists them at the top. Their values have already been moved, so you can delete those lines from .env.

## If the portal will not start

A setting may be preventing startup. On the server, open config/settings.properties in the data directory, correct or remove the relevant entry, then restart the container. Setting changes are recorded in the log by setting name.

diagnostics.title: Журнал и диагностика
diagnostics.summary: Что может администратор и как помочь с сервером
diagnostics.body:
Администратор помогает с сервером: смотрит журнал, проверяет интеграции и собирает данные для разработчика. Данных учеников администратор не видит.

## Разделы

- **Состояние** — плитки: службы, очередь событий, версия и время работы, память и место на диске, последняя копия, адрес портала. Кнопка «Собрать диагностику» вверху скачивает архив для разработчика: журнал и настройки без паролей и личных данных.
- **Журнал** — три фильтра: «Логи» (записи сервера; выберите запись — справа код запроса и подробности ошибки), «События» (внутренние события портала; зависшие можно отправить ещё раз) и «Ошибки». Если запись не выбрана, справа можно временно включить подробные записи для одного раздела.
- **Интеграции** — «Проверка связи» с мессенджерами, ИИ, сервером звонков (LiveKit) и другими сервисами и раздел «ИИ-помощник».
- **Копии** — [резервные копии](/admin/help/backups): создание и восстановление.
- **Настройки** — [настройки портала](/admin/help/settings) вместо файла .env.

Разделы — в панели слева, «Справка» — внизу неё. На телефоне все пять разделов внизу экрана, «Справка» — под кнопкой ☰ вверху слева. Пункт с вашим именем внизу панели слева открывает «Мой аккаунт»: там тема, язык и «Выйти».

## Если что-то сломалось

1. Откройте «Интеграции» и нажмите «Проверить».
2. Посмотрите «Журнал» за нужное время.
3. Нажмите «Собрать диагностику» в «Состоянии» и отправьте архив разработчику.

## На сервере

Если портал поставлен установщиком, на сервере есть команда `teacherbox`:

- `sudo teacherbox status` — запущен ли портал и какая у него версия;
- `sudo teacherbox logs backend` — журнал, если портал не открывается;
- `sudo teacherbox update` — обновить портал до нового выпуска (данные и настройки остаются);
- `sudo teacherbox backups` — скопировать резервные копии в папку на сервере;
- `sudo teacherbox reset` — удалить все данные портала (базу, файлы, копии на сервере, учётные записи) и запустить его как после новой установки; настройки в .env остаются.

HTTPS даёт встроенный Caddy: он сам получает сертификат для домена из настройки TEACHERBOX_DOMAIN. Если сертификата нет, проверьте, что домен указывает на сервер и порты 80 и 443 открыты (`sudo teacherbox logs caddy`).

backups.title: Резервные копии и адрес портала
backups.summary: Как администратор делает и восстанавливает копии и меняет адрес портала
backups.body:
## Копии

Раздел «Копии»: список копий, «Создать копию сейчас» и восстановление. Скачать копию может только учитель — в копиях данные учеников. Google Диск для копий подключает учитель. В разделе «Копии» видны и копии на Google Диске: перенесите нужную на сервер и затем восстановите её из общего списка.

Копии хранятся столько дней, сколько задано в «Настройки» → «Резервные копии» → «Сколько дней хранить копии» (по умолчанию 14); более старые копии любого вида портал удаляет после создания новой — на сервере и в Google Диске.

Чтобы восстановить копию:

1. Нажмите «⋮» в строке копии → «Восстановить…».
2. Введите пароль администратора.
3. Дождитесь итога: портал сделает копию текущего состояния, перезапустится и восстановит выбранную.

После восстановления войдите с паролем, который действовал на момент копии. Предупредите учителя: всё, что добавлено после копии, пропадёт.

Для перезапуска у контейнера должна быть политика `restart: unless-stopped` (она есть в файлах compose портала). Без Docker копия восстановится при следующем запуске.

## Адрес портала

«Состояние» → плитка «Адрес портала». С него начинаются все ссылки портала: приглашения, сообщения ботов, подписка на календарь, адреса возврата Google и Яндекса. Если адрес задан переменной TEACHERBOX_PUBLIC_URL, в портале он только показывается.

settings.title: Настройки портала
settings.summary: Файлы, прокси, вход и резервные копии — без перезапуска
settings.body:
«Настройки» собраны в карточки: «Файлы в заданиях», «Сеть и прокси», «Вход и сеансы», «Сообщения», «Резервные копии». Под значением видно, откуда оно взято: «по умолчанию», «из .env» или «задано здесь».

## Изменить

1. Измените нужные значения — они отметятся «изменено».
2. Нажмите «Сохранить» и введите пароль администратора.
3. Почти все настройки начинают действовать сразу, без перезапуска. Если под полем написано «Применится после перезапуска портала», портал перезапустится сам — на минуту он будет недоступен всем.

Значения, заданные здесь, важнее файла .env. Кнопка «Вернуть как в .env» убирает своё значение.

Резервные копии портала и досок делаются раз в день: переключатель включает или выключает копию, рядом выбирается время в часовом поясе учителя. Если в .env задано другое расписание в формате cron, оно показывается как есть, и его можно поменять.

Новые сроки входа и блокировки действуют со следующего входа — открытые сеансы не прерываются.

## Только в .env

Карточка «Только в .env» показывает текущие значения того, что здесь не меняется: домен, порт и ресурсы контейнера, звонки, учётные записи, секрет токенов, журнал, перезапуск после восстановления. Пароли и секреты не показываются — только «задан» или «не задан». Чтобы поменять такую настройку, выполните на сервере sudo teacherbox config: откроется файл .env, а после сохранения портал перезапустится с новыми значениями. Если такая настройка была сохранена в портале раньше, кнопка «Убрать сохранённое» возвращает значение из .env.

## Перенесено в настройки учителя

Часовой пояс, валюта, правила занятий, адрес портала, боты и подключения Google теперь задаёт учитель в своих «Настройках». Если в .env остались их переменные, портал перечисляет их вверху страницы: значения уже перенесены, строки можно удалить из .env.

## Если портал не запустился

Скорее всего, какое-то значение мешает запуску. Откройте на сервере файл config/settings.properties в папке данных, исправьте или удалите строку и перезапустите контейнер. Все изменения записаны в журнал с именами настроек.

login.title: Sign-in, password and profile
login.summary: Set up your account, reset your password and update your profile
login.body:
## Set up your account

Your teacher will send you an invitation link. Open it and choose a username and password. You can then sign in to the portal with those details. If the invitation has expired or does not open, ask your teacher for a new link.

## Reset or change your password

If you have forgotten your password, ask your teacher for a password reset link.

To change a password you know, select your name at the bottom of the sidebar, then “Change password”. On a phone, open the ☰ menu to find your account.

## Update your photo and name

Select your name to open “My account”. Your photo and name are under “Profile”; on a phone or tablet, select the row with your name.

- **Photo:** in the “Photo” row, choose “Upload” and select a JPEG, PNG or WebP image. The portal crops it to a square and resizes it. Your teacher sees it alongside your name throughout the portal. Use the bin button to remove it.
- **Name (“What should we call you?”):** enter the display name you want to use in the portal. Your teacher will still see the name they entered for you. Leave this field blank and save to use that name again.

schedule.title: Schedule and rescheduling
schedule.summary: Find your lessons, request a new time or report an absence
schedule.body:
“Schedule” shows your lessons in a week or month view. On a phone it opens in agenda view: choose a day in the week strip to see its lessons. Tap a lesson to see its time, topic, boards and meeting link.

On a computer, upcoming lessons and “My requests” appear beside the calendar. On a phone, lesson details open in a panel at the bottom of the screen.

## Request a change

Choose “Reschedule” or “Cancel” beside the lesson. To reschedule, suggest a new date and time. You can also include a message for your teacher.

Times when your teacher is unavailable are marked “Busy”. Choose a free time; the portal will tell you if your suggested time is unavailable.

Your teacher will receive the request and you will be notified of their response. Check its status in “My requests”. Until your teacher responds, you can withdraw it with “Withdraw” or “Withdraw request”.

A late cancellation may be charged as a missed lesson. A request for a recurring lesson applies only to the date you selected.

## Group lessons

If you cannot attend a group lesson, choose “I can’t attend”. Let your teacher know in advance so you will not be charged for your absence.

## Lesson summaries

When your teacher sends a summary, you will receive a “Lesson summary” notification. Open the lesson and read “What we covered”. Completed lessons are also listed in “Lesson history” on the Schedule page. You can turn off summary notifications in “My account”.

## Add lessons to your own calendar

In “Calendar subscription”, choose “Get subscription link” and add the link to your calendar as a subscription. Lessons will update automatically. You can also get the link through a [messaging bot](/cabinet/help/bot).

lesson.title: Lessons and boards
lesson.summary: Join a lesson, use the call controls and open shared boards
lesson.body:
## Join a lesson

Choose “Join lesson” on your home page or in the schedule. Your next lesson appears first on the home page, with its date, start time and duration. Shortly before it starts, the card shows a countdown; during the lesson, it shows the time remaining. Once a lesson has started, you cannot request to reschedule or cancel it.

For a portal call, check your camera and microphone in the preview, allow browser access when prompted, then choose “Join”. During the call you can:

- turn your microphone and camera on or off;
- drag your camera preview to another corner;
- choose “Minimise” to keep talking while you use a board or work on an assignment;
- choose “Expand” to return to the full call window;
- choose “Leave call” to leave.

If your teacher uses an external video service, such as Telemost, the lesson link opens that service in a new tab.

## Open a board

Open “Materials” → “Boards” to see boards shared with you or your group. Search by title or filter by “All”, “In the portal” or “External”. The next lesson card also links directly to its boards.

An **Excalidraw board** opens in the portal. You and your teacher can draw together and see each other’s cursors. Changes are saved automatically. The status at the top shows “Saved”, “Saving…” or “Offline — reconnecting…”. Images appear as they load, so you can start drawing straight away.

The board menu (☰) contains the theme, grid and mouse-wheel settings. Choose “Zoom” or “Scroll (touchpad)” to suit your device. Use “Back” to return to where you opened the board, or “Back to boards” if you followed a direct link. These actions are also in the board menu.

To save reusable shapes, select them, right-click and choose “Add to library”. Open your library with the button at the top right.

An **external board**, such as Holst, opens in a new tab. The bot also provides “Join lesson” and “My boards” links.

homework.title: Homework
homework.summary: Read assignments, submit your work and respond to feedback
homework.body:
## Find an assignment

Open “Homework”. On a computer, the list is on the left and the selected assignment opens on the right. On a phone, select an assignment to open it, then use the back arrow to return to the list.

Assignments are grouped by what to do next; empty groups are hidden:

- **Sent back for revision:** your teacher left a comment, shown under the title;
- **To do:** the nearest deadline first, with the days left (or how long it is overdue);
- **Handed in:** work in review and accepted work with its grade.

On a phone, an “Up next” card at the top opens the returned work or the assignment due soonest. Each entry shows the title, due date and status. Overdue assignments are marked in red. The number on the Homework menu icon counts assignments you still need to submit. You will receive a reminder before a deadline.

Your home page also lists outstanding assignments under “To hand in”, with the nearest deadline first. Choose “Revise” for returned work. Recent feedback appears under “Reviewed recently”.

## Videos and textbooks

Videos play within the assignment when supported; other links open in a new tab. If your teacher has shared a transcript, choose “Transcript” below the video.

Attached textbooks appear under “Textbooks”, with the relevant page numbers. Select a title to open it or use the download button to save the assigned pages.

## Submit your work

1. Open the assignment.
2. Write your response in “My answer”, right under the task. “Photo of your notebook” (it opens the camera on a phone) and “File” attach photos and documents; use “Remove” to take one off. The portal checks the file type and size when you select them.
3. Choose “Hand in”.

Text you have typed but not handed in is kept on this device, so you can leave the page and come back to it (the note says “draft saved”). Files are not kept in the draft; attach them again. On a phone “My answer” stays at the bottom of the screen, with the materials and the test below the task.

Your teacher can accept the submission, add a grade and feedback, or return it for revision. Reviewed work opens in the same place as the assignment. Accepted work shows your grade, your teacher’s feedback, any quiz mistakes and “Next assignment”; your own answer is folded under “My answer”. Returned work shows the feedback, your previous attempt and a new one: the text of your previous answer is already copied in, so add what is missing, attach your files again and choose “Hand in again”.

## Take a quiz

If an assignment includes a quiz, a “Quiz” card next to it shows how many questions and attempts you have. Choose “Start the quiz” and it fills the screen, one question at a time. Questions may ask you to select answers, enter text or a number, match pairs, or put items in order. Use the arrow buttons for ordering questions; until you move an item the question counts as skipped, though an order that is already correct still scores as it stands.

Move between questions with “Back” and “Next”, or jump to one by its number; answered numbers are filled in. Answers save as you go, so you can close the quiz with the cross and pick it up later with “Continue the quiz”. When you are done, choose “Finish the quiz”. If you skipped any questions, you will be asked to confirm. You cannot change that attempt afterwards.

Your score appears immediately. Depending on your teacher’s settings, correct answers and explanations appear immediately, after the due date, or are not shown. If more attempts are allowed, choose “Try again”. Your best score counts.

When you are ready, choose “Hand in” so your teacher can review your work and quiz result.

## Work on a board

If your teacher has added an assignment to a board, choose “Go to board” at the top of the assignment. Its text and textbook pages will already be there. Submit your response on the assignment page as text or a file.

textbooks.title: Textbooks
textbooks.summary: Open and download textbooks and workbooks shared by your teacher
textbooks.body:
Open “Materials” → “Textbooks” to find textbooks, workbooks and other resources shared with you or your group. Each card shows a cover and title. Group resources also show the group’s name.

Search by title or use “All”, “Textbooks”, “Workbooks” and “Other” to filter the list.

Select a title to open the file in a new tab. Word documents download instead. Use the download button to save a copy.

A textbook disappears from this list if your teacher stops sharing it with you or you leave the group it was shared with.

billing.title: Payments
billing.summary: Check your balance, lesson price and payment history
billing.body:
“Payments” shows your balance, lesson price and transaction history. Filter the history to see all transactions, payments only or lesson charges only.

- **Credit** is money you have paid towards future lessons.
- **Outstanding balance** is the amount still to pay for past lessons.
- **History** lists lesson charges and recorded payments, with dates and amounts. The latest 20 entries appear first; choose “Show more” for older entries.

A lesson is charged when your teacher marks it completed or missed without notice. Your teacher records payments after receiving them.

If a payment has a receipt, use its receipt button to open it. HEIC images download instead of opening in the browser.

Contact your teacher if a payment or charge does not look right.

bot.title: Messaging bots
bot.summary: Get notifications and manage lessons through Telegram, VK or MAX
bot.body:
## Notifications in the portal

The bell at the top of the page opens your notifications. Its badge shows how many are unread. New notifications appear first; read notifications are grouped under “Read”. Open that group to see them.

Open a notification, mark it as read, or choose “Mark all as read”. On a phone, swipe a notification left or right to mark it as read.

## Connect a messaging app

Select your name → “Notifications” → “Where to send” → “Connect” beside the app you use. You can also use the connection card on your home page. Open the bot chat and press “Start”, or send the code shown in the portal.

The bot uses your account language. Notifications include an “Open” button for the relevant portal page or a “Join” button for a lesson. If the messaging app cannot display a link button, the link appears as text.

## Use the bot

Send /menu to see the available actions:

- **Schedule:** upcoming lessons and meeting links;
- **Join lesson** and **My boards:** quick links;
- **Cancel a lesson** and **Reschedule a lesson:** send a request to your teacher, or report that you cannot attend a group lesson;
- **My requests:** pending requests, which you can withdraw, and resolved requests;
- **Payments:** your balance and recent payments.

The bot asks for confirmation before sending a request. Choose “Cancel” or send /cancel to stop an action. Enter times as 18:30 and dates as 05.10.

## Device notifications

You can receive lesson reminders, new assignments and teacher messages on your phone or computer even when the portal is closed. You can use these alongside messaging app notifications.

Select your name → “Notifications” → “Where to send” → “This device” → “Connect”, then allow notifications in your browser. Enable them separately on each device and browser. Turn a device’s switch off to remove it.

On iPhone and iPad, first add the portal to your Home Screen using Share → Add to Home Screen, then open it from that icon. Device notifications require HTTPS. The portal explains if your browser does not support them.

Notifications pass through Google, Mozilla or Apple services. Their content is encrypted with your device’s key, so those services cannot read it. Your notification topics and quiet hours apply to both device and messaging app notifications.

## Turn notifications off

Send /stop to the bot or disconnect the app in “My account”. You can also choose notification topics (“What to send”) and quiet hours there; changes save immediately.

appearance.title: Mobile use, theme and language
appearance.summary: Use the portal on your phone and choose your theme and language
appearance.body:
## Use the portal on your phone

The portal works in your phone’s browser. To give it its own app icon in Chrome on Android, open the browser menu (⋮) → “Add to Home screen” → “Install”. It will open in a separate window.

The bottom bar contains “Home”, “Schedule”, “Homework”, “Materials” and “Payments”. Open ☰ at the top left for Help and your account. On a computer, these sections are in the sidebar.

Your home page starts with your next lesson and “Join lesson”. Below it you will find assignments to submit, recent feedback, your lesson credit and materials. On wider screens these appear in two columns.

Select a list entry to open its details. Forms with several fields open full screen, with the main action at the top right. If you close a form with unsaved changes, choose “Discard” to lose them or “Cancel” to keep editing.

Errors appear below the relevant field. If a section fails to load, choose “Retry”. You can also use a keyboard: Tab moves between controls and Esc closes dialogs and panels.

## Choose a theme

Select your name → “Appearance”, then choose “Light”, “Dark” or “System”. Your choice is saved on this device.

## Choose a language

In the same Appearance section, choose “Русский” or “English”. You can also choose a language below the sign-in or invitation card before signing in.

Your choice is saved on the device and in your account. New notifications, bot replies and calendar subscriptions use that language. Your teacher’s messages and lesson content remain as they wrote them.

login.title: Вход, пароль и профиль
login.summary: Как войти в кабинет, сменить пароль, фото и имя
login.body:
## Первый вход

Учитель присылает ссылку-приглашение. Откройте её, придумайте логин и пароль — и вы в личном кабинете. Дальше входите на странице входа с этим логином и паролем.

## Забыли пароль

Попросите учителя прислать ссылку для сброса пароля. По ссылке задайте новый пароль.

## Сменить пароль

Пункт с вашим именем (внизу панели слева, на телефоне — под кнопкой ☰) → «Смена пароля».

Если ссылка не открывается или устарела, попросите учителя прислать новую.

## Фото и имя

Пункт с вашим именем (внизу панели слева, на телефоне — под кнопкой ☰): фото и имя — в разделе «Профиль». На телефоне и планшете нажмите строку со своим именем.

- **Фото** — в строке «Фото» нажмите «Загрузить» и выберите картинку (JPEG, PNG или WebP). Фото видно вам и учителю в портале. Корзина рядом убирает фото.
- **Как к вам обращаться** — как портал обращается к вам в кабинете. Учитель по-прежнему видит вас под тем именем, которое указал сам. Сотрите своё имя и сохраните, чтобы вернуть имя от учителя.

schedule.title: Расписание и перенос
schedule.body:
Нажмите на занятие в расписании, чтобы посмотреть время, тему, доски и ссылку на урок. Там же можно попросить перенос или отмену.

В «Расписании» можно выбрать «Повестку», неделю или месяц. На телефоне сначала открывается «Повестка»: выберите день, чтобы увидеть его занятия. Ближайшие занятия и ответы учителя на запросы доступны на этой же странице.

## Отменить или перенести занятие

Откройте занятие и нажмите «Перенести» или «Отменить». Для переноса предложите удобное время. При необходимости напишите комментарий учителю.

Время, когда учитель занят или не работает, помечено «Занято». Выберите свободное время: попросить перенос на занятое нельзя.

Учитель получит запрос и ответит — ответ придёт в уведомлении, а статус виден в блоке «Мои запросы». Пока учитель не ответил, запрос можно отозвать кнопкой «Отозвать» у занятия (на телефоне — «Отозвать запрос» в панели занятия).

Если отменяете поздно, учитель может засчитать занятие как пропуск.

Запрос переноса или отмены относится только к выбранному занятию, даже если оно повторяется каждую неделю.

## Итоги урока

Когда учитель отправит итоги, придёт уведомление «Итоги урока». Их можно прочитать в карточке занятия («Что прошли»), а все проведённые занятия собраны в списке «История занятий» на странице «Расписание». Тему уведомлений можно отключить в «Моём аккаунте».

## Групповые занятия

Если не можете прийти на занятие группы, нажмите «Не приду». Если предупредили заранее, учитель сразу узнает, что вас не будет, и это занятие не оплачивается.

## Календарь в телефоне

Блок «Подписка на календарь» → «Получить ссылку» → добавьте её в календарь телефона как подписку. Занятия будут появляться там сами.

То же самое можно сделать через бота в мессенджере ([Бот](/cabinet/help/bot)).

lesson.title: Урок и доска
lesson.summary: Как войти в звонок и открыть доску
lesson.body:
## Войти на урок

Перед уроком нажмите «Войти в урок» на главной странице или в расписании. Карточка ближайшего занятия показывает время начала, а во время урока — сколько осталось. Перенести или отменить начавшееся занятие нельзя.

Звонок идёт прямо в портале. Перед входом откроется окно: проверьте камеру и микрофон (браузер спросит разрешение — разрешите) и нажмите «Войти». В звонке можно выключить микрофон или камеру, окошко со своей камерой можно перетащить в другой угол, а «Свернуть» оставит звонок в маленьком окне — откройте доску или задание, разговор продолжится. «Выйти из звонка» — красная кнопка.

Если учитель задал ссылку на другую видеосвязь (например, Телемост), кнопка откроет её в новой вкладке.

## Доски

Доски, которые учитель открыл вам или вашей группе, — в разделе «Материалы», вкладка «Доски»: карточки с картинкой доски, фильтры «Все», «На портале», «Внешние» и поиск по названию. Нажмите на карточку, чтобы открыть доску. Доски ближайшего занятия — кнопками прямо в его карточке на главной: нажмите, чтобы открыть.

- **Доска Excalidraw** открывается прямо в портале на весь экран. Рисуйте вместе с учителем: доска сохраняется сама, штрихи учителя появляются у вас сразу, виден его курсор с именем. В меню доски (☰) внизу — тема, сетка и что делает колесо мыши: «Масштаб» или «Прокрутка (тачпад)». Вверху видно, сохранено ли («Сохранено», «Сохранение…», «Нет связи — повторим»). Картинки доски появляются по мере загрузки — рисовать можно, не дожидаясь их. Вернуться — «← Назад» (туда, откуда вы открыли доску) или «← Доски», если доску открыли по ссылке; то же — в меню доски (☰). Нужные фигуры сохраняйте в свою библиотеку: правой кнопкой → «Добавить в библиотеку», открыть — кнопкой «Библиотека» справа вверху.
- **Внешняя доска** (например, Холст) открывается в новой вкладке.

Ссылки на урок и доски можно получить и в боте: «Войти на урок» и «Мои доски».

homework.title: Задания
homework.summary: Как посмотреть и сдать домашнее задание
homework.body:
## Посмотреть задания

В разделе «Задания» работы собраны по группам: «Вернули на доработку» — учитель оставил комментарий, его видно под названием; «Сделать» — ближайший срок первым, рядом написано, сколько осталось дней (или что срок прошёл); «Сдано» — работы на проверке и принятые с оценкой. Пустые группы не показываются. На телефоне сверху карточка «Ближайшее» с кнопкой «Открыть» — вернувшаяся работа или задание с самым близким сроком. Нажмите на задание, чтобы открыть его. На телефоне стрелка «назад» возвращает к списку. Просроченные задания помечены, а число на значке «Задания» в меню показывает, сколько работ ждёт вашей сдачи. Перед сроком придёт напоминание.

На главной задания к сдаче собраны в блоке «Сдать» (ближайший срок первым; у возвращённого работа — «Исправить»), а последние проверенные — в блоке «Проверено недавно».

Если в задании есть видео, оно играет прямо в задании (ссылку на другой сайт откройте кнопкой «Открыть видео в новой вкладке»). Если учитель открыл расшифровку, под видео есть кнопка «Расшифровка».

Если к заданию привязан учебник, он есть в задании, в блоке «Учебники», со страницами. Нажмите на название — откроются только нужные страницы; кнопка со стрелкой их скачивает.

## Отправить работу на проверку

1. Откройте задание.
2. В блоке «Мой ответ» под текстом задания напишите ответ. «Фото тетради» (на телефоне открывает камеру) и «Файл» прикрепляют фото и документы; лишнее уберите кнопкой «Убрать». Слишком большой файл или файл не того типа портал отклонит сразу при выборе.
3. Нажмите «Сдать».

Напечатанный, но не сданный текст сохраняется на этом устройстве: можно уйти со страницы и вернуться — он на месте (подпись «черновик сохранён»). Файлы в черновике не хранятся, их прикрепите заново. На телефоне блок «Мой ответ» закреплён внизу экрана, а материалы и тест идут под текстом задания.

Учитель проверит работу: примет её с оценкой или вернёт на доработку с комментарием. Проверенная работа открывается там же, где задание. У принятой — оценка, комментарий учителя, ошибки теста и кнопка «Следующее задание»; ваш ответ свёрнут в «Мой ответ». У вернувшейся — комментарий, ваша прошлая попытка и форма новой: текст прошлого ответа уже скопирован, допишите недостающее, прикрепите файлы заново и нажмите «Сдать снова».

## Тест в задании

Если в задании есть вопросы, рядом с ним появится карточка «Тест» — сколько вопросов и попыток. Нажмите «Начать тест»: тест откроется во весь экран, по одному вопросу. Выберите вариант, впишите короткий ответ или число, для «соответствия» выберите пару к каждой строке, а в «порядке» расставьте элементы кнопками со стрелками (пока вы ничего не сдвинули, вопрос считается пропущенным, хотя верный порядок и так засчитается как есть). Между вопросами переходите кнопками «Назад» и «Дальше» или номерами вопросов: отвеченные номера закрашены. Ответы сохраняются сами — можно закрыть тест крестиком и потом нажать «Продолжить тест». В конце нажмите «Завершить тест»; если какие-то вопросы остались без ответа, тест переспросит. После этого попытку изменить нельзя. Сразу видно «Лучший результат: N из M». Верные ответы и пояснения учитель показывает сразу, после срока сдачи или не показывает вовсе. Если попыток несколько, «Пройти ещё раз» начнёт новую, засчитывается лучшая. Когда всё готово, нажмите «Сдать» — учитель увидит ваш результат.

## Задание на доске

Если учитель поместил задание на вашу доску, вверху задания есть кнопка «Перейти на доску» — там уже лежат текст задания и страницы учебника. Ответ всё равно сдавайте в задании: текстом или файлом.

textbooks.title: Учебники
textbooks.summary: Учебники и рабочие тетради от учителя
textbooks.body:
Учебники — вкладка раздела «Материалы» (рядом вкладка «Доски»): учебники, рабочие тетради и другие материалы, которые учитель открыл вам или вашей группе. Каждый — карточка с обложкой (первая страница) и названием; фильтры — «Все», «Учебники», «Рабочие тетради», «Другое»; у учебника группы указана её название.

Нажмите на название, чтобы открыть учебник в новой вкладке (файл Word скачается), а кнопка со стрелкой скачивает его. Поле «Поиск по названию» помогает найти нужный учебник. Учебник пропадёт из списка, если учитель закроет к нему доступ или вы выйдете из группы.

bot.title: Бот в мессенджере
bot.summary: Уведомления и действия в Telegram, ВКонтакте или MAX
bot.body:
## Уведомления в кабинете

Нажмите на колокольчик, чтобы открыть уведомления. Число на нём показывает, сколько непрочитанных. Откройте уведомление, отметьте его галочкой или нажмите «Прочитать все». На телефоне проведите по уведомлению пальцем влево или вправо, чтобы отметить его прочитанным. Прочитанные уведомления доступны в свёрнутом разделе «Прочитанные» — нажмите на него, чтобы открыть.

## Подключить

Пункт с вашим именем → «Уведомления» → «Куда присылать» → «Подключить» у мессенджера (или «Подключить» в карточке на главной). Откроется чат с ботом — нажмите «Запустить» или отправьте ему показанный код.

## Кнопки в уведомлениях

Под уведомлением — кнопки: «Открыть» ведёт на нужную страницу портала, «Подключиться» — на урок. Если мессенджер не принимает такие кнопки, ссылка придёт текстом: «Открыть: …».

## Что умеет бот

Напишите боту /menu:

- **Расписание** — ближайшие занятия и ссылка на урок;
- **Войти на урок** и **Мои доски** — ссылки;
- **Отменить занятие** и **Перенести занятие** — запрос учителю (в группе — «Не приду»);
- **Мои запросы** — запросы, ждущие ответа (их можно отозвать); решённые (согласован, отклонён) — под кнопкой «Решённые»;
- **Оплаты** — баланс и последние оплаты.

Перед отправкой запроса бот переспрашивает. «Отмена» или /cancel прерывают действие. Время пишите так: 18:30, дату — 05.10.

## Уведомления на телефоне без мессенджера

Напоминания о занятиях, новые задания и сообщения учителя могут приходить системными уведомлениями телефона, даже когда кабинет закрыт, — без мессенджера или вместе с ним. Пункт с вашим именем → «Уведомления» → «Куда присылать» → «Это устройство» → «Подключить» (или «Включить» в карточке на главной) и разрешите уведомления в запросе браузера. выключатель в списке убирает устройство. Темы и тихие часы те же, что для мессенджеров.

На iPhone и iPad уведомления работают только в приложении на экране «Домой»: «Поделиться» → «На экран “Домой”», затем откройте кабинет с нового значка. Нужен HTTPS-адрес портала; если уведомления недоступны, карточка объяснит причину. Уведомление проходит через сервис Google, Mozilla или Apple — текст зашифрован ключом вашего устройства, сервис его не читает.

## Отключить

Отправьте боту /stop или отключите мессенджер в «Моём аккаунте» (пункт с вашим именем в панели слева). Там же, в «Что присылать», можно выбрать темы и «Тихие часы». Изменения сохраняются сразу.

appearance.title: Телефон и тема
appearance.summary: Как пользоваться кабинетом с телефона, включить тёмную тему и выбрать язык
appearance.body:
## С телефона

Кабинет работает в браузере телефона, ничего устанавливать не нужно. Чтобы добавить отдельный значок в Chrome на Android, откройте меню браузера (⋮) → «Добавить на главный экран» → «Установить». Затем открывайте кабинет с этого значка.

- На телефоне разделы «Главная», «Расписание», «Задания», «Материалы» и «Оплаты» доступны внизу экрана, «Справка» — под кнопкой ☰. На компьютере разделы и справка находятся в панели слева. Число у «Заданий» показывает, сколько работ ждёт сдачи.
- «Отмена» в окне закрывает его и ничего не меняет.
- На главной — ближайшее занятие, задания к сдаче и недавно проверенные работы. «Оплачено N занятий» показывает, на сколько занятий хватит вашего баланса.
- Чтобы присоединиться к ближайшему занятию, нажмите «Войти в урок» на главной.
- Если закрыть форму с несохранёнными правками, портал спросит «Отменить изменения?». «Не сохранять» сбросит правки, «Отмена» вернёт в форму.
- Если поле формы заполнено не так, портал пишет об этом под полем; если блок не загрузился — предлагает «Повторить».
- Кабинетом можно пользоваться с клавиатуры: Tab переходит между кнопками и полями, Esc закрывает окна и панели.

## Тёмная тема

Пункт с вашим именем → «Оформление» → «Светлая», «Тёмная» или «Как в системе». Выбор запоминается на этом устройстве.

## Язык

Там же, в «Оформлении», — «Русский» или «English». На странице входа языки — под карточкой входа. Выбор запоминается на этом устройстве и в аккаунте: на этом языке приходят уведомления, отвечает бот в мессенджере и пишется календарь по ссылке.

first-steps.title: Getting started
first-steps.summary: Set up your teaching space and invite your first students
first-steps.body:
Teacher Box brings your students, schedule, assignments, payments and notifications together.

The first time you sign in, [initial setup](/teacher/help/setup) takes you through your password, name, portal name and address, time zone, currency, lesson price and lesson rules.

## Your first four steps

1. **Add a student.** Choose “Create” → “Student”, or “Students” → “Add student” on a phone. Send the invitation link by email or through a messaging app. The student uses it to choose a username and password.
2. **Connect a messaging app.** Open “Settings” → “Notifications and messengers” → “Connect”. The wizard helps you create a bot for Telegram, VK or MAX so you can receive reminders and student requests.
3. **Connect the AI assistant** if you want it. It drafts assignments, quizzes and feedback, and you always edit the result. You need a key from an AI provider: “Settings” → “AI”.
4. **Schedule a lesson.** Choose “Create” → “Lesson”. Set “Repeat” to once or every one to four weeks.

You already chose the default lesson price during setup. To give one student a different price, open their “Profile” tab.

The “Getting started” checklist under “To do” on your home page tracks these steps and hides completed ones.

## Your Today page

Your next lesson appears first, with its time, duration, topic, boards and “Start lesson” button. The button changes to “Join lesson” while the lesson is running. Before and during a lesson, the card shows a countdown or the time remaining. After it ends, the next lesson appears automatically.

- **Lessons today** lists the day’s lessons and their status, with the next one highlighted.
- **To do** brings together lessons awaiting an outcome, student requests, submissions to review and outstanding balances. Choose “Completed” or “Missed” to record an outcome; for groups, record attendance. Long lists show a count of additional items.
- **The monthly summary** shows payments received this month and outstanding balances.
- **Week** summarises completed lessons, absences, assignments set and work submitted on time, from Monday to Sunday.

Use “Create” in the sidebar for common actions. On a phone, the + button on Today offers the same choices; other sections have their own action button.

Next: [Students and invitations](/teacher/help/students), [Schedule and requests](/teacher/help/schedule), [Payments](/teacher/help/billing).

setup.title: Initial setup
setup.summary: The first-sign-in wizard: your details, time and payment, lesson rules
setup.body:
Initial setup opens the first time you sign in. Every step already has a sensible default, so you can simply select “Next” each time. You can change everything later in Settings.

1. **Password:** this step appears only if the portal generated your first password, which was written to the server log. Choose your own; this step cannot be skipped.
2. **You and your portal:** enter the name students will see, and a photo if you like. The portal name appears in navigation, browser tabs, the sign-in page and the calendar. The portal address is the one students use to open it, such as https://school.example.com. Invitations, bot links and calendar subscriptions start with it. The portal fills in the address you are using now, and “Check” tells you whether it can be reached.
3. **Time and payment:** the time zone sets your schedule and monthly reports, and the portal suggests the one on your device. Then choose a currency, the usual lesson length and the default price for new students and groups. Individual prices can be changed later.
4. **Rules:** late cancellation, lesson reminders, the reminder before an assignment is due, and how many weeks of a repeating lesson appear ahead. An example next to each rule shows what it does.
5. **Done:** the portal suggests what to do next: add a student, connect a messaging app, the AI assistant or Google Calendar. “Go to the portal” opens your home page.

“Back” returns to the previous step. “Next” saves the step. “Skip” leaves the step’s values as they were and moves on. If a step cannot be saved, it stays open.

## Address warnings

- A localhost address works only on the computer running the portal.
- A home or office network address works only within that network. Students need an address they can reach over the internet.
- An HTTP address sends passwords without encryption. Ask the server administrator to enable HTTPS.

## Changing things later

- Name, logo and colours: “Settings” → “Portal”.
- Time zone, currency, price, lesson length and rules: “Settings” → “Lessons”.
- Your name and photo: “My account”.
- The public address: ask the portal administrator.

Messaging apps, the AI assistant and Google Calendar are not part of the wizard. Connect them in Settings, or from “Getting started” on your home page.

students.title: Students and invitations
students.summary: Add students, manage their details and control portal access
students.body:
## Add a student

1. Choose “Create” → “Student”, or “Students” → “Add student” on a phone.
2. Select “Student” and enter their name. Email and phone are optional and visible to you and the student.
3. Copy the invitation link and send it to the student. Their Profile tab opens so you can add a private note, default topic, colour, lesson price and video meeting link.

The student chooses a username and password using the invitation. Links expire after a few days; generate a new one if needed.

## Find a student or group

Students and groups share one list. Search by name or filter by “All”, “Groups” or “Deactivated”. Archived groups also appear under Deactivated.

A student’s entry shows their photo or initials, name, next lesson and balance. Outstanding amounts are highlighted in red. “Invited” and “Deactivated” identify accounts that are not active. Hover over an invitation status to see its expiry date.

Select an entry to open its details on the right. On a phone, details replace the list; use the back arrow to return.

## Student details

The header shows the student’s name, when they joined, connected messaging apps and balance. “Message”, “Payment” and “Lesson” let you contact them, record a payment or schedule a lesson.

- **Overview:** upcoming lessons, outstanding assignments, recent transactions, messaging apps and the video meeting link. If no messaging app is connected, send a connection reminder.
- **Lessons:** individual and group lessons, split into upcoming and past. Recurring lessons are grouped; choose “Show all dates” to expand them. Rescheduled and cancelled lessons appear separately. Past lessons show the outcome and, for groups, the student’s attendance. Upcoming lessons cover the next six months. History loads 20 lessons at a time; choose “Show more” for older entries.
- **Homework:** assignments and their status, with outstanding work first and accepted work below. Select a title to open it.
- **Payments:** balance, total charges, total payments and transaction history. See [Payments](/teacher/help/billing).
- **Profile:** name, email, phone, private note, default topic and colour. Save these fields together. The lesson price has its own Save button; video meeting changes apply immediately. “Portal access” shows the read-only username and invitation or reset link details.

You always see the name you entered for the student, even if they choose a different display name for their account.

## Invitations and access

Open the student’s Profile tab to manage access:

- **New invitation** creates another link before the student has activated their account.
- **Reset password** creates a reset link for an existing account.
- **Deactivate account…** prevents sign-in while keeping lesson, payment and homework history.
- **Restore access** lets a deactivated student sign in again.

## Student tags

Tags are your private notes on a student, such as English level, school year or goal. Only you see
them; students and bots do not.

1. Open “Settings” → “Students” → “Student tags” and create a tag with a name and ordered values.
   If every student needs their own words, such as hobbies, choose “Free text”; it needs no
   values. An empty list offers templates: CEFR level, “Year group”, “Goal” and “Interests”. You
   can’t change a tag’s type while any student has it.
2. Keep “Use in AI” on if tasks, quizzes and reviews should adapt to the value.
3. On the student’s Tags tab, choose a value; it is saved straight away. Free text, up to 120
   characters, is saved when you press Enter or leave the field; clearing the field removes the
   tag. “What the AI will see” shows what the assistant receives.
4. In the student list, choose “Tags” and a value to show only those students. Free-text tags
   are not available as filters.

When you ask the AI for a draft, “What I know about the students” chips appear above the request. Remove a chip
with “×” to leave that tag out of this request. If the chosen students have different values or
texts, the chip is highlighted: select it and pick one. If all the texts together run over 120
characters, the AI gets the most common one until you pick another. If your request asks for something else, the AI follows
your request. Deleting a tag or a value clears it for every student, and this cannot be undone.

## Student colours

Choose one of ten colours, or “No colour”, on the Profile tab. The colour marks avatars, calendar lessons and selection chips throughout your view of the portal. Students do not see it.

Scheduled lessons use the student’s colour. Completed, missed and cancelled lessons use their status colour, with the student’s colour as a stripe along the edge.

For shared teaching, see [Groups](/teacher/help/groups). Boards are under [Materials](/teacher/help/boards).

groups.title: Groups
groups.summary: Teach several students together and manage their shared lessons
groups.body:
A group brings together students who attend the same lessons. Its lesson price is charged separately to each member.

## Create and manage a group

1. Choose “Create” → “Student”, or the add button in Students on a phone, then select “Group”.
2. Enter a name, select the students and choose “Create”.
3. Set the price per student on the group’s Profile tab. You can also add a default topic and colour.

Groups appear in the Students list with a group icon, member count and next lesson. Use the Groups filter to find them.

Select a group to open its details. “Message” contacts every member and “Lesson” schedules a group lesson. The ⋮ menu contains “Archive” or “Restore from archive”.

- **Overview:** upcoming lessons and the room link.
- **Lessons:** upcoming and past group lessons and their outcomes.
- **Homework:** members’ assignments, with each student’s name and status.
- **Members:** add or remove students. Select a name to open that student’s details.
- **Profile:** name, default topic, colour, price per member and video meeting link.

## Attendance and membership

Choose the group when scheduling a lesson. All members will see it. After the lesson, record who attended and who missed it. Students who attended or were absent without notice are charged. Students who reported an absence in advance are not charged.

Membership changes apply to upcoming lessons. Past lessons keep their original participants.

Archive a group when you stop teaching it. Upcoming lessons are cancelled and the history is kept. Find archived groups under the Deactivated filter.

schedule.title: Schedule and requests
schedule.summary: Schedule lessons, set time off, record outcomes and respond to requests
schedule.body:
## Schedule a lesson

Choose “Create” → “Lesson”, or “Schedule” → “Lesson” on a phone. Select a student or group, date, time and duration. A title, topic and video meeting link are optional.

If the title is blank, the student or group’s name is used. A default topic from their Profile tab fills the title when you select them; you can change or clear it. The separate Topic field describes that particular lesson and is not copied across a recurring schedule.

Set “Repeat” to once or every one to four weeks. The selected date determines the weekday. An end date is optional. By default, you can see the next 12 weeks of recurring lessons; later dates appear automatically.

## Use the calendar

On a computer, choose a week or month view and use the mini calendar to jump to another day. Student requests and time off appear beside it. Filter lessons by student or group above the calendar; additional filters appear under “N more”.

On a phone, the schedule starts in agenda view with a week strip and the selected day’s lessons. Switch to Week, Month or Time off above the calendar.

Drag a lesson to suggest a new time, then choose “Reschedule” to save or “Undo reschedule” to put it back. The portal warns about conflicts before saving. In month view, selecting an empty day opens a lesson form at 10:00 with the default duration; adjust both as needed.

## Time off

Open “Time off” to mark a one-off period, such as a holiday, or weekly hours, such as lunch breaks and days off. Weekly periods can have start and end dates. Use 00:00–00:00 for a whole day.

Time off is hatched in the calendar. Edit or delete it from its ⋮ menu. Private labels, such as “Lunch”, are visible only to you.

Students see these periods as “Busy” and cannot request a lesson then. They cannot see your labels or other students’ details. You can still schedule a lesson during your own time off.

## Record outcomes and attendance

Open a lesson and choose “Completed” or “Missed”. The outcome is saved immediately and the lesson is charged accordingly. For groups, choose “Mark attendance” and record each student’s attendance.

An Undo message appears for six seconds after recording an outcome. Choose “Undo” to reverse the outcome and its charge. You can also select the same outcome again to clear it, or select another to change it. For groups, use “Clear outcome” in the ⋮ menu.

Past lessons without an outcome are outlined in red. You can record outcomes from the calendar, the phone agenda or “To do” on your home page.

## Share a lesson summary

Once a lesson has started, add a summary in its details. Summaries are unavailable for cancelled lessons and individual lessons marked Missed.

“What we covered” is visible to the lesson’s students and initially shows the lesson topic. “Next lesson topic” fills the next lesson’s topic if that field is empty. “Save” keeps your changes; “Send to student” or “Send to students” also sends a Lesson summary notification.

If AI is enabled, “Generate draft” uses the lesson topic, assignments and your notes to suggest a summary. Review it before sending. Completed lessons with summaries appear in the student or group’s lesson history. In the bot, choose “Add summary” after recording a completed lesson.

## Cancel, restore or delete

Use “Cancel lesson…” in the lesson’s ⋮ menu to enter a reason, say whether the student requested it and decide whether to charge. The lesson remains in the calendar, crossed out, and the student is notified. “Restore” reinstates it and notifies the student again; a conflict warning appears if the time is now occupied.

Deleting removes a lesson from the schedule, calendars and reports. Only scheduled or cancelled lessons can be deleted; clear a completed or missed outcome first. Deleting an upcoming scheduled lesson sends a cancellation notification.

When editing, cancelling or deleting a recurring lesson, choose “Only this lesson” or “This and future lessons”. The portal shows how many lessons will change. The boundary follows the original date, even if a lesson has been rescheduled. Completed, charged, cancelled and individually edited occurrences are preserved. Deleted occurrences are not generated again.

## Respond to student requests

Students can request a reschedule or cancellation in the portal or bot. Requests appear in “Student requests” and arrive as notifications with “Approve” and “Decline” buttons. In the portal, open a request to respond.

- **Reschedule:** approve the suggested time or enter another. The portal warns about lessons, time off or Google Calendar events at that time; you can choose to proceed.
- **Late cancellation:** decide whether to mark the lesson as missed and charge for it.
- **Decline:** include a reply, for example to suggest another time.

A group member’s advance notice that they cannot attend is approved automatically.

calls.title: Calls
calls.summary: Run video lessons in the portal with permanent student and group rooms
calls.body:
Each student and group has a permanent call room. Calls run in the browser without installing an app. Check availability under “Settings” → “Lessons” → “Calls”; room links appear in student and group details.

## Join a call

Choose “Start lesson”, follow a room link or open a reminder. In the preview, check your camera and microphone, choose devices or turn them off, then select “Join”. Allow camera and microphone access when your browser asks.

## Call controls

- **Microphone and camera:** turn either on or off. A red, crossed-out control means it is off.
- **Your preview:** in a two-person call, drag your camera preview to another corner. The portal remembers the position.
- **Share screen:** on a computer, share a window, browser tab or entire screen.
- **Settings:** change devices or adjust echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain control. These are on by default; try turning them off if audio sounds clipped or muffled. Your choices are saved.
- **Connection details:** inspect each participant’s connection quality, protocol, ports, delay and audio loss. Share these details with the administrator when investigating poor audio.
- **Minimise:** keep the call in a small movable window while using boards, assignments or other portal pages. On a phone it becomes a bar above the bottom navigation. “Expand” restores the full window.
- **Leave call:** leave using the red button.

## External meeting links

An external link, such as Telemost or Zoom, takes precedence over the portal room. To use portal calls again, remove it from the student or group’s Profile tab under “Video meeting”. See [Video meetings](/teacher/help/meetings).

The administrator must configure the call server before portal calls are available.

meetings.title: Video meetings
meetings.summary: Use an external video service for a student or group
meetings.body:
You can give a student or group a permanent Telemost, Zoom or other meeting link. Lessons, reminders and “Join lesson” will use it instead of the built-in [call room](/teacher/help/calls).

## Add or remove a link

Open “Students”, select the student or group, then open “Profile” → “Video meeting”. Create a meeting in your video service, paste its link and choose “Add link”. Changes in this section are saved immediately.

“Send to student” sends the link to the student’s account and connected messaging app. Without an external link, it sends the portal room link. Remove the external link to return to portal calls.

## Open a meeting

Choose “Start lesson” in the lesson details. On Windows, Telemost can open in its app. Use the arrow beside the button to choose “Open in browser” instead. This preference is saved on your computer and can be changed under “Settings” → “Lessons” → “Calls” with the “Open Telemost in the app” switch.

You can override the permanent link for a single lesson in its details.

boards.title: Boards
boards.summary: Create shared boards, draw together and add lesson materials
boards.body:
Open “Materials” → “Boards” to see your boards. Search by title, student or group, filter by “All”, “In the portal” or “External”, and change the sort order.

- **Excalidraw boards** run in the portal, support live collaboration and save automatically.
- **External boards**, such as [Holst](https://app.holst.so), are links to another service and open in a new tab.

## Create and share a board

1. Choose “Create” → “Board”, or “Materials” → “New board” on a phone.
2. Choose a type and enter a title. For an external board, paste its link and enable link sharing in that service.
3. Select students and groups. Remove a selection chip to revoke that selection. All current group members can access a shared group board; students who leave the group lose that access.

Board cards show a preview, title, recipients and last update. Select a card to open it. Use its ⋮ menu to edit or delete it. Deleting an Excalidraw board also deletes its content, images and board backups. Lesson cards link to the relevant student or group’s boards.

## Draw together

An Excalidraw board opens full screen. Participants see each other’s drawings, cursors and names live. If two people edit the same shape, the latest change wins. Images load gradually so you can start drawing immediately.

The top status shows “Saved”, “Saving…” or “Offline — reconnecting…”. If the live connection drops, the portal retries and checks for changes periodically.

The board menu (☰) contains:

- **Theme:** Light, Dark or System, shared with the portal theme setting;
- **Grid:** visible to everyone on this board;
- **Mouse wheel:** Zoom, or Scroll (touchpad). In scroll mode, pinch or use Ctrl to zoom. This preference is saved on your device.

Use “Back” to return to the page you came from, or “Back to boards” after opening a direct link. The portal waits for unsaved changes and the preview to be saved before returning. If you are offline, it asks whether to leave without saving. Closing the browser or tab may interrupt saving.

## Reuse shapes

Select shapes, right-click and choose “Add to library”. Open the library at the top right and drag saved shapes onto any board. Each user has a separate library, available across their devices. To import an .excalidrawlib file, use the library’s ⋯ menu → “Open”. The external library catalogue is not available within the portal.

## Board backups

Changed boards are backed up daily; the last seven daily backups are kept. Before major edits, open “Backups” from the board menu or card’s ⋮ menu and choose “Make a backup”. You can keep up to 20 manual backups per board.

Restoring a backup saves the current board first, so you can restore it later. Students with the board open see the restored content automatically.

## Add materials to a board

Choose “Add to board” from an assignment, its editor or a submission review. Search for a board and choose “Text” for editable text or “Image” for a fixed rendering, useful for formulae and tables. Assignments offer boards shared with their students or groups.

Excalidraw boards open in a new tab with the material already added. An assignment is placed in a frame with its title and today’s date, followed by attached images and textbook pages. PDF and Word attachments remain on the assignment page.

For external boards, the material is copied to the clipboard. Paste it with Ctrl+V, or Cmd+V on a Mac. Copying images requires HTTPS.

You can also add [textbook pages](/teacher/help/textbooks) from Materials or an attached textbook. Pages are arranged in a framed row on an Excalidraw board.

homework.title: Homework
homework.summary: Create assignments, review submissions and give feedback
homework.body:
## Create an assignment

1. Choose “Create” → “Assignment”, or “Homework” → “New assignment” on a phone. The editor opens with just the essentials: recipients, the text, the due date and the material buttons.
2. Choose who gets the assignment and write the text; its first line becomes the title. Set the due date with “By the next lesson”, “In a week”, “No deadline” or “Pick a date…”. Add textbooks, files, a photo, videos, a quiz or a board with the buttons under “Materials”. As soon as you start typing, the assignment saves itself as a draft with the students you chose; if you leave without writing anything, nothing is created. Markdown supports bold text, lists and links; use Preview to check the result. The “AI assistant” button opens the assistant beside the text.
3. Under “To”, add students and groups. Students in more than one selected group receive the assignment once. Removing a group keeps any students also selected individually. “By the next lesson” sets the due date to the start of those students’ next lesson; pick another option if you prefer.
4. Textbooks, files, videos and a board appear in the assignment only once you add them. Add textbooks and files with the buttons under “Materials”; they show as one list. Select a name to open it (PDFs and images open in a new tab). Add a video or a board from the “Add” group in the menu on the left (on a tablet, or with the AI assistant open, use the “Video” and “Board” buttons under “Materials” instead). “Board” opens a list of your boards: the one you choose shows in the Board section (the × clears it), and once the assignment is given out the “Add to board” window opens with that board selected. A quiz is not a material: add questions on the Quiz tab. You can remove anything you added, and empty sections take up no room.
5. For a video, use “Video” (up to five) and paste a link: the video appears as a tile. YouTube, Rutube and VK videos play within the assignment; other links open in a new tab. Students see the videos in the order of the tiles, so drag them to reorder. Each tile shows whether it has a transcript and whether students can see it. Select the settings button on a tile to open the video in a window over the editor (full screen on a phone). There you can rename the video, import YouTube captions (if several tracks are available, choose one from the menu), load an .srt or .vtt file, edit the transcript or remove the video. The arrows move between the assignment’s videos without closing the window. Changes are saved straight away, so “Done” and Esc just close it. The AI uses the transcript; students see it only if “Show transcript to students” is enabled.
6. Choose “Assign”. Students are notified once the materials are ready and reminded before the due date. You return to where you opened the editor (the list or the assignment); “Open” in the “Assignment created” message takes you to the assignment. There is no separate draft button: once the assignment has a title, the draft saves itself a couple of seconds after each change, and the header shows when it was last saved. You can leave the editor at any time without losing anything.

“Assign and add to board” creates the assignment, then lets you place its text, images and textbook pages on a board. The assignment remembers the board and gives students a “Go to board” button. “Add to board” on the assignment page has the same effect.

## Manage assignments

“Edit” opens the editor. It has two tabs: Instructions, for recipients, the due date, the text and materials; and Quiz, for the questions and quiz settings. On a phone these are Instructions, Questions and Settings. If the assignment has a quiz, Instructions shows a summary: the first questions, the number of questions, points and attempts, and “Open quiz”. On a wide screen a list of sections on the left scrolls to the one you choose. A draft keeps its students under “To” and you can change them. You can also add or remove its textbooks and files in the editor, and it saves itself. An issued assignment shows its students without “×”, and “Assign to more” adds new ones. Its textbooks and files are updated on the details page, and “Save” keeps your changes; the portal checks before you leave without saving. “Back” returns to the page you opened the editor from.

“Make a copy” creates a draft with the original text, files, textbooks and videos, but no recipients or due date. The editor opens so you can adapt it.

The Homework page lists assignments on the full width. Search by assignment title or student name, and use “For” to select a student or group. Search and “For” are kept in the page address.

- **Active:** assignments with work still outstanding, grouped by due date: Overdue, This week, Later and No due date.
- **Drafts:** assignments you have not given to anyone yet.
- **Done:** assignments with all submissions accepted. Use “Show more” after the first 20.

Each row shows the materials in the assignment (textbooks, files, questions, videos, board), who it is for, the due date, how many submissions are in and the status. On a tablet the table becomes tiles with an icon, the title, who it is for and when it is due, a progress bar (“3 of 4”) and the status. On a phone it becomes cards and the views become chips.

Select an assignment to open it on its own page; the arrow returns you to the list.

## The “By student” view

The “List · By student” switch at the top of the Homework page shows a whole week at once: students are the rows and the assignments due that week are the columns. The arrows next to the dates move between weeks, and “For” narrows the grid to one student or group. The colour of a cell tells you what to do: green is accepted (with the grade), yellow is waiting for your review (a quiz shows its score), red is overdue or sent back, grey means the student has not handed it in yet, and a dashed cell means the assignment was not given to them. The last column counts the work handed in.

Select a yellow cell to review that piece of work, or a dashed one to open “Assign to more students” with the student already chosen. Any other cell, or a column title, opens the assignment. The view you pick is kept in the page address.

## Assignment details and textbooks

The header shows the title, the number of students with the deadline, “Edit” and “Review N submissions” (hidden when nothing is waiting). The review button opens the first submission; “Next” in the review panel moves on to the following one. The “⋮” menu holds “Create copy”, “Add to board”, “Open board” (once the assignment is on a board) and “Delete…”.

Each student has a card on the left: when they handed in (“Handed in today at 09:12”, “Accepted yesterday · grade 4”, “Sent back for revision on 28.10”), the status, the start of the answer, the quiz score and the number of files. “Review” opens a submission that has been handed in; “Open” opens any other, and “Remind” (for students who have not handed in or are revising) sends the student a notification — no more than once an hour. Counts above the cards show how many are accepted, waiting for review and sent back. “Assign to more” gives the work to other students or groups.

On the right you will find the instructions (long text is folded to three lines until you choose “Show all”), videos, files and textbooks. Select a name to open a file or textbook in a new tab, or use the arrow button to download a file. Change the text, files and textbooks with “Edit”. For an assignment with a quiz, “Mistakes by question” appears below: each question has a bar and a count such as “3 of 4”, showing how many students got it wrong.

On a wide screen the instructions take the main column: the full text, the materials as one list and the quiz line. Students sit in a narrow column on the right, grouped under To review, Sent back, Not handed in and Accepted (empty groups are hidden). Each row has one button — “Review”, “Remind” or “Open” — and selecting a student’s name opens their work. “Assign to more” is the person icon at the top of the column, and “Mistakes by question” sits below the students.

On a phone these become the tabs “Students · Assignment · Mistakes” (“Mistakes” only with a quiz), and “Review N submissions” stays at the bottom of the screen.

In the assignment editor (“Edit” on the assignment page), choose “Textbook” under Materials to select a resource and pages, such as 12-14, 20. Leave pages blank for the whole textbook. Students can access the assigned pages even if the full textbook is not shared with them. Word documents are downloaded in full, with page numbers provided for reference. The pencil changes the pages; the cross removes the attachment. See [Textbooks](/teacher/help/textbooks).

“Open board” in the “⋮” menu opens a linked board. “Delete…” in the same menu removes the assignment, submissions and files; recovery requires a portal backup.

## Add a quiz

Questions are on the editor’s Quiz tab. The list on the left shows each question’s number, type and points. Select a question to open it on the right. To reorder, drag the handle or focus it and use the up and down arrow keys. “Question” below the list offers six types:

- **Single choice** and **Multiple choice:** mark the correct options.
- **Short answer:** list accepted answers; press Enter after each one. Capitalisation, extra spaces and the difference between ё and е are ignored.
- **Number:** enter a correct answer and an optional tolerance.
- **Matching:** enter pairs; the right-hand column is shuffled for students.
- **Ordering:** enter the correct order; students receive shuffled items.

“With AI” opens the AI assistant. In an open question you can change its type, duplicate it, move it or remove it. Options carry over between single choice, multiple choice and ordering; for other changes the portal asks first. Options can be dragged too, and pressing Enter in the last option adds another. Each question has points from 1 to 100 (1 by default) and an optional explanation; choose “Answer explanation” to add one. Matching and ordering award all points or none. “Student view” at the top opens the quiz the way your student takes it: full screen, one question at a time. You can try the answers; nothing is saved. On the right, “Quiz settings” sets when answers are revealed and how many attempts are allowed: 1, 2, 3 or unlimited. The best attempt counts. “Summary” shows the number of questions, the points and roughly how long the quiz takes. On a phone, the Questions tab shows only the list: tap a question to open it full screen, use the arrows at the bottom to move between questions, and use “Question” at the bottom to choose the type of a new one. A draft keeps unfinished questions as they are, but you can’t assign it until they are complete. The portal opens the Quiz tab, marks those questions in red and lists them under “Summary”. Once a student starts the quiz, questions are locked; the rest of the assignment remains editable. To change the questions, choose “Duplicate to edit”: the portal copies the assignment and opens the copy’s Quiz tab.

The AI assistant can draft questions. On the Quiz tab it prepares questions straight away; on Instructions it drafts the text. You can still switch with “What to prepare”. Append the draft or replace all questions, and review them before assigning.

Reviews show the best quiz attempt, incorrect answers first, with an answer key. Use “Mark correct” or “Mark incorrect” to override automatic marking. The score fills the grade field unless you enter a grade yourself. “Mistakes by question” on the assignment page highlights common errors. A completed quiz is enough for a student to submit the assignment for review.

## Review a submission

Submissions waiting for review sit in the “To review” strip at the top of the Homework page: each card shows the student, the assignment, when it was handed in, a “Late” tag and the quiz score. “Review” opens a submission; “Review them all” starts with the oldest and moves on to the next after each decision. When none are left you return to where you started and see “Nothing left to review”. “Review” on an assignment’s page goes through that assignment’s submissions only, and “Back” returns to the assignment. You will see the assignment, the student’s response and attached images. “Open on the board” opens the assignment’s board.

Add feedback and a grade, then choose “Accept” or “Return for revision”. Quick comments help with common responses. “Next: …” opens the next submission after your decision. If AI is enabled, “AI draft” suggests feedback and a grade; review them before choosing “Insert”.

On wide screens the review form sits beside the submission. On a phone, use the bottom toolbar; feedback, grades and AI drafts open in a bottom panel. Existing direct links to submissions and the review queue still work.

textbooks.title: Textbooks
textbooks.summary: Upload resources, share them with students and use selected pages
textbooks.body:
“Materials” → “Textbooks” stores textbooks, workbooks and other resources, with one file per entry. Supported files are PDF, Word (DOC or DOCX) and images, up to 100 MB.

## Add a textbook

1. Choose “Create” → “Textbook”, or open the Textbooks tab and choose “New textbook”.
2. Select a file. The filename provides an initial title; edit it as needed.
3. Choose Textbook, Workbook or Other, and optionally enter a course. Existing course names are suggested.
4. PDF pages are counted automatically and an image counts as one page. You can enter a page count for a Word document.
5. Select students and groups to share it with. Remove a chip to deselect a recipient, or clear the selection. Group sharing includes all current members.

## Open and manage resources

Search by title and select a resource to open it. PDFs and images open in the browser; Word files download. The ⋮ menu provides:

- **Download:** save the original file.
- **Edit:** change its type, title, course, Word page count and sharing.
- **Add to board:** place PDF pages or an image on an Excalidraw board. Enter a range such as 12-14, up to 30 pages at once. Pages appear in a frame to the right of existing content; move the frame to move them together. Word documents cannot be added this way. From an assignment, only its students’ boards are offered; from Textbooks, you can choose any board.
- **Replace file:** upload a corrected version. PDF pages are counted again.
- **Delete…:** remove the textbook and its file, including its attachments to assignments.

Students find shared resources under Materials and can download them. For assignment-specific page access, see [Homework](/teacher/help/homework).

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.summary: Draft assignments, quiz questions, feedback and lesson summaries
ai.body:
The AI assistant produces drafts for you to review. You decide what to save and send.

## Create a draft

In the assignment editor, open “AI assistant” and describe what you need. Choose “Generate”, then review the result. “Replace” uses the draft title and text; “Append” adds the text after your own; “Discard” dismisses it; “Regenerate” requests another version. Drafts are not saved automatically.

On wide screens, the assistant opens beside the editor. On smaller screens it opens in a dialog. Closing it or resizing the window preserves your instructions, selected sources and draft. The Text/Preview switch changes the view of the same Markdown field.

## Choose source materials

Use “Source materials” to select attached textbook pages, PDFs and images: up to five files and 20 pages at once. Files selected for a new assignment can be used before saving it. Word documents are not supported as sources.

Videos with transcripts are also available as sources. The AI reads the transcript, rather than watching the video, and can refer to timestamps such as [1:05]. If the video is not listed, add a transcript in its settings first: import YouTube captions or load a file.

Select “Questions” under “What to prepare” to draft quiz questions. Review them in the editor before saving.

## Reuse prompts and draft feedback
